question: What is the primary bloodborne virus transmitted by unsafe injections worldwide?
explanation: Hepatitis B virus, along with hepatitis C and HIV, is a primary bloodborne pathogen transmitted through contaminated injection equipment. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T10#GNS122_U3_T10_h1)

question: How does the World Health Organization define a safe injection?

options.A: Any injection given by a registered nurse using a new plastic syringe
options.B: A painless procedure requiring no skin preparation or disposal bins
options.C: One that causes no harm, poses no provider risk, and creates safe waste
options.D: An intravenous medication dose administered strictly in a sterile theater

explanation: The WHO definition covers three areas: recipient safety, healthcare provider safety, and proper waste management. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T10#GNS122_U3_T10_h1)

question: What is the first pillar of the WHO injection safety framework?

options.B: Immediate recapping of all used needles

explanation: Reducing unnecessary injections by choosing oral medications when possible is the primary strategy to lower overall exposure risks. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T10#GNS122_U3_T10_h2)

question: Why does the WHO promote using single-use disposable syringes?

options.A: To speed up medication administration on busy wards
options.B: To reduce the financial cost of purchasing metal autoclaves
options.C: To eliminate the need for puncture-resistant disposal boxes
options.D: To completely prevent cross-contamination from reused equipment

explanation: Single-use devices ensure that pathogens cannot be transferred between patients via contaminated syringes or needles. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T10#GNS122_U3_T10_h2)

question: When should a nurse perform hand hygiene during medication administration?

options.A: Only after discarding the used syringe
options.B: After finishing the entire ward round
options.C: Only when hands are visibly bloody

explanation: Hand hygiene is mandatory before handling injection equipment to prevent introducing pathogens to the patient. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T10#GNS122_U3_T10_h3)

question: Which action breaks sterile technique during an injection setup?

options.A: Wiping the medication vial top with alcohol
options.B: Using a new disposable syringe for the patient
options.C: Performing hand hygiene prior to procedure
options.D: Touching the needle shaft with bare fingers

explanation: The needle shaft must remain sterile. Touching it with bare fingers transfers microorganisms directly into the tissue. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T10#GNS122_U3_T10_h3)

question: What is the main feature of an Auto-Disable syringe?

options.A: It locks permanently after a single use
options.B: It filters out air bubbles from the syringe barrel
options.C: It automatically recaps the needle after injection
options.D: It dilutes medications without human intervention

explanation: Auto-disable syringes have a built-in mechanism that prevents the plunger from being pulled back or reused. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T10#GNS122_U3_T10_h4)

question: Why is reusing a disposable syringe on the same patient discouraged?

options.A: It violates hospital budgeting policies regarding plastic waste quotas
options.B: It guarantees that the medication dose will be completely inaccurate
options.C: It increases the risk of bacterial contamination and localized infection
options.D: It causes the plastic barrel to melt from friction during the push

explanation: Even on the same patient, multiple entries into vials or tissues increase the chance of introducing environmental bacteria. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T10#GNS122_U3_T10_h4)

question: At what capacity should a sharps disposal container be closed and replaced?
explanation: Sharps containers must be sealed at 75% capacity to prevent accidental punctures when adding more items. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T10#GNS122_U3_T10_h5)

question: Why is two-handed needle recapping strictly prohibited?

options.A: It bends the needle tip and makes future injections painful
options.B: It slows down medication administration during emergencies
options.C: It is the leading cause of accidental needle-stick injuries
options.D: It damages the plastic seal of the disposable syringe

explanation: Holding the cap with one hand while guiding a sharp needle frequently results in piercing the fingers. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T10#GNS122_U3_T10_h5)

question: What is the first action a nurse must take after suffering a needle-stick injury?

options.A: Cover the puncture site tightly with adhesive tape
options.B: Wash the wound immediately with soap and water
options.C: Fill out an extensive hospital incident report form
options.D: Search for the doctor to prescribe antibiotics

explanation: Immediate washing with soap and running water helps remove blood and lowers the viral load entering the bloodstream. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T10#GNS122_U3_T10_h6)

question: Why must Post-Exposure Prophylaxis (PEP) for HIV be started as soon as possible after exposure?

options.A: To satisfy legal requirements for workplace injury compensation
options.B: To prevent secondary bacterial wound abscesses from developing
options.C: To stop the virus from replicating and establishing systemic infection
options.D: To relieve the severe local pain and swelling at the puncture site

explanation: Early administration of antiretroviral drugs prevents the virus from taking hold in the immune cells. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T10#GNS122_U3_T10_h6)
